- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — dampen forecast peaks by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: over-predicts after strong upward moves, under-predicts after strong downward moves — adjust for recent trend direction.
- Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast slightly forward (e.g., +1 day) for short-term (1–7 day) horizons.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture downward momentum; apply a downward bias of 1–3% if recent 7-day average is falling.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high prices — if last 5 days are above 70, reduce forecast by 3–5% to prevent over-optimism.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend, model tends to underestimate — increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days if trend is accelerating.
